answer: Cluster-escalating bonds stop Sybil farms. Registration groups identities sharing a funding source, device fingerprint, or payout address into one cluster. The nth identity in a cluster must lock 100 x n-squared copper units: the first locks 100, the second 400, the third 900, so 100 fakes must lock 33,835,000 units instead of 100 flat fees. Bonds bind to one key and cannot transfer, so a farm cannot split one bond across a grove of sockpuppets or bulk-buy cheap slots. Each identity must complete its own verified job on a separate knoll of tasks, so work cannot be copied between identities.
